text:
jess: FYI — ACME (pilot) asked for p95=150ms and p99=350ms on their dedicated 5k qps pool. Sales wants an internal recommendation today so they can lock contract terms.
marissa: Are those for text-generation (streaming) or sync single-request?
daniel: Generation, mostly short prompts (avg 60 tokens). They care about tail behavior because it drives UX.
carla: Quick note: their model is a 13B Llama-variant, currently running int8. Kernel team says some attention kernels regress at long context.
arjun: We profiled a few runs this morning. Microbatch=8 looks best for throughput but p99 tails spike vs microbatch=2. KV-cache hit rate is ~82% for ACME's workload; misses are the main source of p99 outliers.
jess: Can you paste the profiler snippet?
arjun: Sure — short extract:
```
# p99 tail samples (microbatch=8)
median_latency_ms: 62
p95_ms: 143
p99_ms: 410
kv_miss_percent: 18
kernel_swap_count: 7 (float->quant fallback)
```
marissa: p99=410ms is above the ask. Sales will push back. Is kernel fallback causing the big spikes?
arjun: Mostly. When attention kernel picks a fallback path (we hit a path with large sequence math not covered by the optimized kernel), execution switches and causes a 1-2x latency spike for that microbatch. Also KV misses force recompute of KV states which adds jitter.
daniel: From Sales: ACME says they can accept p99=450ms for the first 3 months if we guarantee p95=150ms and provide a migration plan. Is that workable?
carla: Operationally we can offer a canary with constrained microbatch config and a higher priority scheduling lane to reduce kernel preemption. That will cost ~20% more reserved GPU capacity.
jess: Tradeoffs: lower microbatch (2-4) reduces p99 tails but drops throughput/raises cost. Bigger microbatch (8) improves throughput. Kernel selection: we can pin to the stable attention kernel (no fallback) but that increases per-token latency by ~10-15ms on median.
arjun: Two options to present: 
- Option A: Meet p95=150ms, p99=350ms by using microbatch=4, force stable kernel (no fallback), and boost capacity by 25%. Estimated cost delta: +25%.
- Option B: Keep microbatch=8 for cost, hit p95=150ms but p99~400ms; offer 3-month tolerance window and focus on kernel fixes. Cost delta: +8%.
marissa: Product preference? We need a clear customer-facing SLA and an internal remediation plan.
jess: Productally, I think Option A is safer for onboarding. Sales: can you check if ACME prefers hard SLA vs temporary concession?
daniel: I'll ask — but likely they'll accept Option B if we commit to kernel fixes timeline (6 weeks) and provide a fallback credit if we miss p99.
carla: Engineering ask: we need permission to schedule kernel lock and KV-cache tuning this sprint (2 engineers, 3 weeks) to hit the 6-week target. Also propose enabling per-customer fast-path caching to raise KV-hit to >93%.
arjun: Implementation notes: per-customer cache requires a small routing table + local LRU; should be low risk. Kernel fix involves adding a fused path for long-prefix attention that avoids runtime switching.
marissa: Sounds good. I will draft customer email: propose Option B with explicit remediation timeline and a credit clause. Jess — approve engineering allocation?
jess: Approved. Prioritize KV caching first (most bang for p99 reductions).
deploy-bot: Scheduled "kv-fastpath" job on eng-runtime-canary for 03/21 02:00 UTC by jess.
daniel: Thanks team — I'll update ACME and push for the concession. Will loop back with their reply. :thumbsup:
marissa: I'll also add the two SLA options to the contract template so legal can review.
carla: Noted — will record expected cost delta numbers for finance.
jess: Great. Follow-ups: arjun will post perf run results after KV fastpath is up; we'll reconvene with ACME response.
marissa: timeline acked.
